Let me look at the `fortran` magic entry more carefully. The regex `!\^[^Cc\ \t].*$` - the `!` is the relation operator (meaning "not"), and the regex itself is `\^[^Cc\ \t].*$`.

Now, the key question is: what regex can match an empty string? Let me look at the `fortran` regex again: `\^[^Cc\ \t].*$`. This requires at least one character after the start of line, so it can't match empty.

Let me look at the `ruby` regex `\^[\ \t]*end([\ \t]*[;#].*)?$` - this requires "end", so it can't match empty.

Let me look at the `perl` regex `\^#!.*/bin/perl([[:space:]].*)*$` - this requires `#!/bin/perl`, so it can't match empty.

Let me look at the `python` regex `\^from[\040\t\f\r\n]+([A-Za-z0-9_]|\\.)+[\040\t\f\r\n]+import.*$` - this requires "from ... import", so it can't match empty.

Let me look at the `java` regex `\^import.*;$` - this requires "import" and ";", so it can't match empty.

Let me look at the `c-lang` regex `\^template[\ \t]+<.*>[\ \t\n]+` - this requires "template<...>", so it can't match empty.

Let me look at the `algol68` regexes:
- `\^PROC` - requires "PROC"
- `MODE[\t\ ]` - requires "MODE"
- `REF[\t\ ]` - requires "REF"
- `FLEX[\t\ ]\*\\[` - requires "FLEX"

None of these can match empty.

# length of seqnm data in bytes is positive
>&0x00          lelong    >0
# length of smpl data in bytes is positive
